summary: This work uses first-principles calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics to investigate how oxygen vacancies in amorphous Al$_2$O$_3$ Josephson junction barriers affect superconducting qubit coherence. Both the coordination environment (2-, 3-, or 4-fold) and concentration of $V_O$ defects are shown to dramatically alter electrical conductivity, which translates to critical current noise and reduced coherence times via $1/f$ noise mechanisms.
motivation: Oxygen vacancies in Al$_2$O$_3$ tunnel barriers are readily generated under irradiation and are a major source of low-frequency noise in superconducting qubits. Understanding how $V_O$ defects with different local structures influence conductivity and charge transport is essential for designing radiation-tolerant quantum devices.
method: A 160-atom amorphous Al$_2$O$_3$ supercell (density 4.04 g/cm$^3$, bandgap 6.84 eV) was constructed via melt-quench AIMD and validated against experiment. Electronic structure and conductivity ($\sigma/\tau$) were calculated using DFT with SCAN for geometry and HSE06 for band structure. Models with 1–9 vacancies of varying coordination were created to isolate defect effects. Decoherence times were estimated from critical current noise using Van Harlingen's $1/f$ framework.
result: Four-coordinated $V_O$ (conventional) reduces conductivity by 23% and produces largest fluctuations ($\Delta\sigma/\sigma_0 = -0.232$), degrading $T_2$ from 1.0 ms to 0.95 ms. Two- and three-coordinated $V_O$ (amorphous-specific) enhance conductivity by 9–19% with smaller fluctuations, yielding $T_2 \approx 0.97$ ms. At high density (9 vacancies), conductivity drops to $7.78 \times 10^{18}$ Ω$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$s$^{-1}$ with $\Delta\sigma/\sigma_0 = -1.40$, reducing $T_2$ to 0.053 ms and nearly suppressing Rabi oscillations within 50 µs.
